patients.label: 81-year-old man with paravalvular leak 5 months after transfemoral TAVR

identity_evidence.quote: We present a case of an 81-year-old man

attribution_limitations: The abstract calls the angiographic leak "mild" while the case text records "1+ PVL"; both are the same angiography result as worded by the authors but the mapping of 1+ to mild is not stated, so it is not applied.

Figure 2A and 2B print three-decimal on-screen caliper values while the text gives the vena contracta area (0.36 cm^(2)) and width (0.5 cm) to fewer decimals; a rounding-level difference with image pixel content, recorded in visual.json only and not a conflict.

The sentences reporting the vena contracta area, flow convergence and circumferential extent do not name the imaging modality; the Figure 2 caption describes echocardiographic planimetry for panel A but does not state these values.

The echocardiographic grade is reported as moderate or severe depending on the parameter (vena contracta area and flow convergence suggestive of severe; vena contracta width and circumferential extent suggesting moderate); this records a parameter-dependent discordance, not a single grade.

Examination documented a regular rhythm, 3/6 end-diastolic and mid-systolic murmurs and clear lungs.
